In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. items.summary: Photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) underpin critical applications in telecommunications, sensing, and high-power laser delivery, yet their design remains a manual, expert-intensive process that couples geometric intuition with deep waveguide physics. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising path toward automating PCF design, but can they truly reason about photonic physics from microscopy images, or do they merely recognize visual patterns? We introduce PCFBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs on the perception, reasoning, and decision steps of the photonic inverse-design loop. PCFBench spans 26 tasks organized into six categories of increasing cognitive demand (Geometry Perception, Physics Understanding, Text Generation, Multi-modal Reasoning, Inverse-Design Decision, and Code Generation), built from over 220K FDTD simulation samples across 18 structurally diverse fiber families. We evaluate both individual VLMs on isolated tasks and multi-agent systems (MAS) on the full sequential pipeline from perception to design. Our results reveal a striking perception-design gap: current models can identify fiber geometry with moderate success, yet consistently fail to translate that visual understanding into physics-aware design actions. Moreover, cascading agents through the pipeline exposes significant error propagation, where upstream perception mistakes compound into downstream design failures. These findings suggest that neither model scaling nor naive agent chaining suffices, and that closing the loop demands explicit physical grounding. PCFBench provides the community with a rigorous, multi-dimensional testbed to measure progress toward AI-assisted photonic engineering. The project is available at https://pcfbench.github.io/.
items.title: PCFBench: How Far Can Large Vision-Language Models Go in Physics-aware Photonic Inverse Design?

items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. The statistical implementation includes regime-specific pilot sizing, independent within-method repetition resampling, shared scenario resampling, and a two-dimensional bootstrap for confirmatory inference. Final-test selection follows a frozen rule combining precision requirements from both regimes with the minimum-detectable-effect requirement for the multi-domain superiority hypothesis. Software contents The archive includes the Python simulator and experimental orchestration code, command-line interface, frozen configuration files, typed intervention specifications, agent prompt and structured-output schemas, statistical analysis procedures, automated tests, freeze manifest, calibration documentation, and four Jupyter notebooks covering protocol execution, pilot sizing, repeated experiments, and economic calibration. Validation and research status The implementation passes 31 automated software and protocol-consistency tests. These tests examine computational correctness, reproducibility, regime restrictions, seed handling, bootstrap procedures, and experimental locking. They do not establish empirical agent performance. This release corresponds to the frozen pre-pilot protocol BAD-420-v0.7-2026-09-11 . The final-test set remains locked until a valid pilot mechanically determines its size. No live API-based agent-performance experiment or confirmatory comparison is included in this release. Consequently, the software does not establish that agentic intervention discovery outperforms, matches, or underperforms non-agentic search. items.summary: Deepwave provides wave propagation modules for PyTorch, for applications such as seismic imaging and inversion. It performs forward modelling and backpropagation, so it can simulate wave propagation to generate synthetic data, or invert for the scattering potential (reverse-time migration, RTM, or its least-squares counterpart, LSRTM), other model parameters (full-waveform inversion, FWI), initial wavefields, or source wavelets. It can also be used inside a larger chain of operations, with forward and backpropagation flowing through the whole chain end to end. You can use your own objective functions, or functions that generate the propagator's inputs, and PyTorch's automatic differentiation calculates how to backpropagate through them. New to seismic/wave-equation terminology? The glossary defines the terms (PML, CFL, Born, FWI, and more) used throughout this README and the rest of the documentation. Deepwave requires Python 3.9 or later and PyTorch 2.4 or later. First install PyTorch for your CPU or CUDA device using the instructions on the PyTorch website . Then install Deepwave: pip install deepwave   macOS wheels support Apple Silicon. Intel Mac wheels are no longer provided: PyTorch 2.4 and newer do not publish wheels for that platform. Prebuilt x86 wheels require AVX2. Older CPUs need a source build; see installation troubleshooting . PyTorch is Deepwave's only dependency. The example scripts under docs/ additionally import matplotlib (to draw their figures) and, in some cases, numpy , scipy (smoothing and filter design), torchaudio (applying those filters), torchvision and geomloss , but those are needed only to run the examples, never by Deepwave itself. To install all of them: pip install 'deepwave[examples]'   The documentation contains examples and instructions on how to install and use Deepwave. You might also like to watch a video summary of Deepwave . Not every propagator supports every option (dimensionality, backend, boundary faces, batching, second-order differentiation, callbacks, ...). See the capability matrix (declared in the code and checked by conformance tests) before assuming a combination works. Why Deepwave Computationally efficient. Deepwave's compiled kernels use a hand-derived adjoint for better performance and lower memory requirements than pure PyTorch implementations. See what Deepwave calculates . Second derivatives are supported, not just first. The scalar, acoustic, and elastic propagators can compute Hessian-vector products (derivatives of gradients); see the Hessian example . Born (linearised) modelling. Model scattered waves from perturbations to a background medium for linearised inversion and imaging. See the torch.func example . Deepwave fits into an ordinary PyTorch workflow. Because propagation is a normal PyTorch autograd Function , it works directly with PyTorch optimisers, DistributedDataParallel over shots, torch.func transforms, and any PyTorch loss function or neural-network model of the input parameters. See the capability matrix for exactly what each propagator supports. Deepwave does not try to be a general symbolic PDE solver, a multi-node HPC code, or a non-differentiable simulation toolkit — see Devito , SPECFEM , and k-Wave respectively for those needs. If you are choosing between wave-propagation packages, see the comparison guide . (Note: the DeepWave-KAUST GitHub organisation, home of the SWEEP package, is unrelated to this project.) Features Supports the 1D, 2D, and 3D constant density acoustic / scalar wave equation (regular and Born modelling), variable density acoustic, elastic, viscoacoustic (single-mechanism SLS attenuation), elastic VTI (anisotropic), and pseudo-acoustic VTI ( deepwave.acoustic_vti , the Duveneck et al. 2008 V_S=0 reduction) wave equations Runs on CPUs and appropriate GPUs The gradient of all outputs (final wavefields and receiver data) can be calculated with respect to the model parameters (wavespeed, scattering potential, etc

items.summary: An autonomous refresh mechanism is not completed by specifying a local exchange map: the same apparatus must reach the exchange, leave it, finish its remaining motion, and deliver its state at the prescribed readout time. We construct this connected late route for one specified preparation in the exact-real interpretation of a frozen classical numerical source. The input is a previously certified twenty-coordinate state after entry into coupled occupancy; its validity and retained preparation history are explicit premises. Source-valid continuation establishes occupancy clearing, physical recovery and courier reversal, complete courier passage, a smooth main-wall excursion, and the remaining main processing. The resulting full state is enclosed at the original exact dyadic readout time, without an independently chosen switch, momentum reset, or deletion of internal phase history. The courier’s completed-square coupling distinguishes canonical momentum from physical velocity. At its frozen right cutoff, canonical momentum is continuous while velocity and the assigned source value have different one-sided traces. The completed spatial exchange differs strictly from the ideal exact-period swap; its small algebraic port residual is distinct from the much wider full-state enclosure. Event-dependent times are composed into a common final clock by retaining the actual remaining duration. The result is a conditional fixed-time completion for the supplied source and preparation, not a time-zero reconstruction, an all-input ideal-model theorem, physical auxiliary attachment, or a second service. Returned local Lean evidence supports selected composition, branch-map, accounting and conditional endpoint results; the cumulative trajectory theorem is not fully formalized.

items.summary: Overview This dataset comprises X-ray CT projection data of a composite plate. The data were acquired in 2009 at beamline I12 of the Diamond Light Source. A total of 5401 projection images were collected with an angular step of 0.033° (180°/5400). The dataset exhibits several imaging issues, making it a useful test case for preprocessing and artefact-correction algorithms: random bright pixels caused by electron scattering, ring artefacts often caused by bright defects on the scintillator, unknown optical distortion, and a possible small tilt of the sample. Image Specifications Projection image dimensions: 4008 × 1000 pixels Acquisition Sequence and Calibration Data - Projections : 5401 images, acquired with an angular step of 0.033° (180°/5400) - Dark-field images : 10 images -  Flat-field images : 60 images, acquired in groups of 10 during the scan — 10 before projection collection began and 10 after projection collection was completed Artefacts and Imaging Issues - Random bright pixels caused by electron scattering - Ring artefacts, often caused by bright defects on the scintillator - Unknown optical distortion - Possible small tilt of the sample The files for example reconstruction without artefact correction are included (assumed rotation centre at 1866.0; 8-bit output volume)
items.title: X-ray CT projection dataset of a composite plate with scintillator and distortion artefacts (Diamond Light Source I12, 2009)

items.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse activation, but storing their expert parameters remains a major memory bottleneck. We introduce GS-MoE, a training-free compression framework that addresses redundancy across and within experts through two compression axes: shared-subspace rank and expert intermediate width. Groupwise low-rank representations capture shared structure across experts while retaining expert-specific projections, and Nyström-based neuron compression reduces intermediate width within each expert. For fixed shared subspaces, we derive per-expert reconstruction-error reductions from the reconstruction objective and use them to guide expert grouping. Budgets are allocated hierarchically using a gradient-free layer-importance score to guide the allocation of rank and width budgets across layers, which eigenvalues and leverage then distribute as non-uniform ranks across groups and intermediate widths across experts. Experiments demonstrate the complementary benefits of compression along both axes, particularly at high compression rates on fine-grained MoE models. On DeepSeek-MoE-16B-Base, at a 60% reduction in total model parameters, GS-MoE retains approximately 90% of the uncompressed model's average reasoning performance, compared with 73% for D$^2$-MoE, while achieving 20% lower out-of-domain perplexity. We provide a code implementation at: https://github.com/cbacary/GS-MoE
items.title: GS-MoE: Training-Free MoE Compression via Groupwise Subspace Sharing and Pruning

items.summary: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) express a model's internal activations in the form of readable text. The verbalizer turns an activation into an English explanation; the reconstructor then converts that explanation back into an activation, and the explanation is considered successful if the round trip brings back the original activation. We claim that this criterion evaluates whether the information is sufficient and does not address descriptive faithfulness. A sentence can contain sufficient information to make it possible to identify an activation even if it wrongly explains what the activation does: in the case of reconstruction, the primary aim is to accurately identify the activations and not to describe them. This issue has the same structure as the chain-of-thought faithfulness problem, in which verbal output that has been trained to go with a process is taken as a report on that process, and it parallels the dissociation between an individual's introspective report and the actual governing process as documented in human psychology. Although proposed as interpretability tools for the purpose of alignment, NLAs reintroduce, through unverified explanations, the epistemic problem that they were intended to resolve.
items.title: Natural Language Autoencoders Identify Without Explaining

items.summary: PGA-G v1.0.0 — Research Software and Experimental Evidence This release provides the original research implementation and reproducibility resources for PGA-G: Selective Adaptation and Conformal Calibration for Speech Deepfake Detection . PGA-G introduces a selective adaptation framework that determines when a frozen speech deepfake detector should be adapted using unlabelled deployment data and a genuine-speech reference. The proposed methodology integrates prevalence-based adaptation gating, consistency screening, and conformal calibration to support reliable operating decisions under changing deployment conditions. Research Contributions Selective adaptation: A prevalence-based gate determines whether the deployment data provide sufficient evidence to consider adaptation. Consistency screening: A guard evaluates the adapted scoring branch to reduce reference-dependent shortcuts. Conformal calibration: A genuine-reference calibration procedure establishes operating points under the specified calibration assumptions. Cross-detector evaluation: Experiments examine SSL-AASIST, XLSR-Mamba, and AASIST on ASVspoof 2021 DF and ASVspoof 5. Release Contents The repository includes the research implementation, pre-registered experimental protocols, per-repetition evaluation records, machine-readable numerical results, provenance information, automated tests, and reproducibility documentation. Reproducibility and Verification The included verification framework supports independent examination of the archived experimental evidence, including: 160/160 confirmatory numerical comparisons. 20/20 additional numerical consistency checks. Byte-identical regeneration of the source-grouped numerical summary. Automated file-integrity validation and regression testing. Reconstruction of condition-level experimental evidence from archived results. These checks run without requiring GPU access, pretrained model checkpoints, or original speech recordings. Full detector inference and complete experimental repetition require separately obtained upstream resources and additional environment-specific setup, as documented in the repository. Research Artifact Scope This release serves as a companion research software and experimental evidence archive. It does not distribute the journal manuscript, publication figures, original speech recordings, or third-party pretrained model weights. The repository provides an independently inspectable foundation for evaluating the PGA-G methodology and its reported experimental findings.
items.title: PGA-G: Selective Adaptation and Conformal Calibration for Speech Deepfake Detection

items.summary: This preprint examines how space-themed socioscientific issues (SSI) connect scientific understanding with social and ethical judgment, and how these connections can inform science and STEM education. Drawing on 1,316 educational reports—58 space-related and 1,258 non-space-related—the review combines comparative mapping with detailed examination of space contexts. It addresses four interconnected areas: the representation and educational forms of space-themed SSI; disciplinary knowledge and reasoning; historical, present and future perspectives; and teaching approaches, student responses and learning outcomes. The evidence encompasses learner research, curriculum and teacher education, educational reviews and supporting contributions. Manuscript.pdf — Complete preprint manuscript. Presents the conceptual framework, review methods, findings across the four research questions, discussion, educational implications and references. All main-text figures and tables are included. Word and HTML copies, if supplied, are alternative formats of the same manuscript. S1_Methods_and_Evidence_Tables.pdf — Supplementary methods and selected evidence tables. Explains the search and selection procedures, eligibility criteria, analytical units, coding definitions and weighting methods. It also documents temporal reconstruction and sensitivity analyses, selected science–society reasoning cases, pedagogical evidence, quantitative comparisons and source-identification qualifications. S2_Report_Evidence_Catalogue.html — Searchable report evidence catalogue. Provides searchable and filterable report-level information, including educational scope, Earth–space connections, disciplinary knowledge, epistemic reasoning, teaching practices, outcomes and temporal interpretation. Bibliographic references, source links and selection reasons connect the synthesis to its supporting evidence. Download and open the file in a web browser. S3_Analysis_Data.xlsx — Analysis data workbook. Contains 26 worksheets documenting search strategies, selection decisions, report characteristics, coding definitions, teaching and outcome evidence, temporal coordinates and model parameters, relationships between reports, and the distributions underlying the analyses.
items.title: Distant Worlds, Shared Questions: A Systematic Review of Space-Themed Socioscientific Education

items.summary: Overview This dataset comprises parallel-beam X-ray CT projection data of a cylindrical composite-material bar, together with a reconstructed volume. items.summary: Nine years after its introduction, the transformer remains the default sequence model. The usual explanations are real: parallel matrix multiplication on accelerators, predictable returns to scale, a co-evolved ecosystem and exact recall from an uncompressed context. But they do not explain why most modifications barely move accuracy, which properties are essential, why the changes practice adopted took the forms they did, or where the design can still move. This paper is the entry point to a collection of papers that treat a token-mixing layer as an averaging operator rebuilt from its own input and iterated through depth. Such a layer faces six failure modes (collapse to consensus, contamination of content by routing, runaway feedback, the inability to abstain, dilution as context grows, and the inability to represent direction). Each has a protection, proved within a declared class, and a signature measured at small scale when that protection is removed; for gain control, which protects against runaway feedback, that signature is synthetic. We read softmax attention in a pre-normalized residual block as the one known point where all six protections are cheap at once under the prices of parallel hardware and gradient descent; this is an interpretation, not a measured optimum. Two mechanisms, measured at small scale, help explain why its neighbourhood is flat: trained networks compensate local deficits through spare capacity, and, in ten scored tests, making a protection explicit did not beat a block that already supplies it. The anchor, the residual or input path that protects against collapse to consensus, is the one protection whose loss compensation provably cannot repair: under strict mixing, where repeated averaging contracts token differences toward zero, no extra capacity of bounded gain (bounded sensitivity) brings back what is lost without it, and in small-model ablations nothing else in the block made up for it. This is a proved bound; a trained test that adds capacity is pending. Many changes adopted in the mixing layer and its block since 2017, among them pre-normalization, QK-norm, sinks and output gates, read as re-supplies of the same protections; the account is silent on others, such as changes to the MLP. The room that remains for the design to move is where a protection is patched (met only by a fix that works over a limited range, such as the trained length) or paid at a price that another design could avoid. It includes abstention and retrieval at long context, governed by a two-sided log-N law in the context length (with bounded scores, no fixed rule for abstaining keeps both as the context grows), and bounded memory, whose price for exact recall is a per-head capacity. It also includes decisions that sum over all competitors where reading the largest would do, and the writer of new features (in a transformer, the MLP and the output map), for which the collection has no theory yet of what a good writer computes. Along the way the collection establishes results that stand on their own: attention has an arrow that default statistics of a single operator cannot see; depth is a distribution over path lengths; converged adaptive averaging can amplify changes in its input and overturn correct predictions; and softmax obeys length laws that decisions on maxima escape while the competing scores stay below the decision's threshold. We state what is proved, what is measured, what is interpretation, and what is still pending. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. Please read it with that in mind: the work will be refined further, and later versions will appear under this record. It belongs to a collection released together on Zenodo: the entry paper The Transformer Abides, the monograph A Spectra
items.title: The Transformer Abides: What Attention Needs, and Why It Endures

items.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on role-specific prompts and execution models to solve complex tasks collaboratively. However, prompt optimization typically keeps model assignments fixed, leaving differences in role requirements and their associated inference costs outside the search. We present UniMASO, a Unified framework for heterogeneous Multi-Agent System Optimization through the joint adaptation of prompts and model assignments. UniMASO evaluates candidate updates through local, downstream, and global feedback, using cost-aware Pareto search to retain useful quality-cost trade-offs. Topology-aware co-evolution then coordinates these updates according to agent roles and dependencies. Cross-level trajectory memory further supplies historical successes and failures to guide subsequent optimization. Experiments on five benchmarks and five execution topologies show that UniMASO achieves competitive task performance at substantially lower deployment cost than the strongest homogeneous configurations. Under centralized execution, it improves the average score from 69.79 to 70.40 while reducing token-weighted deployment cost by 85.2% relative to DeepSeek-V4-Pro with MASPO. These results support joint prompt-model adaptation as an effective approach to efficient multi-agent collaboration. The code is available at https://github.com/Achilles008/UniMASO_main.
items.title: Not Every Agent Needs the Strongest Model: Unified Prompt-Model Optimization for Heterogeneous LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: We conduct a version-pinned, reproducible forensic audit of the public Einstein Elevator data package (Zenodo: 10.5281/zenodo.15167723) to determine whether it supports validation of quantum sensor certificates. Through an exhaustive cross-file sliding-window correlation search over 44,207,922 comparisons and exact six-decimal rounding checks, we find that all 31 exported sensor channels have a unique best match within the enumerated raw traces under the stated protocol. Residual numerical differences are highly consistent with text-based absolute quantization; the correlation-loss approximation 1 - r ≈ δ² / (24σx²) is diagnostic for this dataset, not a universal proof. We inspect the MATLAB-derived 318-point population series and reconcile it with a 2022 workbook entry only at the level of counts. An archive-wide search of 181 file objects and 1,654 MATLAB metadata fields finds no documented join key linking the 2022 run-indexed population series to the 2017 timestamped traces under the enumerated search protocol. Using Fréchet-Hoeffding bounds and a Charnes-Cooper linearization, we establish that the public archive does not supply the joint observations needed to identify the EKF false-safe risk without additional coupling assumptions; the formal program is illustrative and is not populated with empirical failure/acceptance coefficients because the required linked observations are absent. We frame this as a bounded data-contract limitation for downstream statistical validation, not as a failure of the original experiment.
items.title: A Reproducible Provenance Audit of the Public Einstein Elevator Data Package: Trace Correspondence, Metadata Linkage, and the Non-Identifiability of Sensor-Certificate Risk from the Public Archive

items.summary: A sequence-mixing layer that is iterated through depth and rebuilt from its own input faces six failure modes. Each is met by a protection—anchoring, alignment, gain control, abstention, a routing budget, or an arrow—with an operator-level statement proved within a declared class, a signature when it is removed, and a price. We organize attention designs as a lattice of kernel, dynamical, and block constraints in which relaxing a constraint buys a capability and obliges a re-supply. We read softmax attention inside a pre-normalized residual block as the lattice point where every protection is either supplied or cheaply re-supplied under parallel-hardware and optimization pricing: of the deficits tested, all but the anchor's were compensated by capacity elsewhere in the deeper models, and explicit protection knobs did not beat the block, both measured at small scale, while corner structure, by which designs would jump rather than drift, remains a hypothesis. The lattice reads the selected adopted changes to the mixing layer, its normalization and its residual path over the last decade as cheap re-supplies of protections, and it locates the room for change. The clearest room is abstention, governed by a two-sided log-N law: with a bounded logit scale, no null keeps both abstention and single-key retrieval as context grows, and tempering the entire logit budget with log N keeps both when its margins are strictly separated. A controlled pilot follows the law, while a prespecified test of its sink prediction on an open production model was undecided by its prespecified rule; descriptively its slopes leaned toward compensation through position, in which position encoding holds the background's growth down. In a prespecified trained harness of 125M-parameter language models, tempering every logit by log N / log N_train on top of YaRN, which already carries a log-length temperature, did not keep abstention and raised long-context perplexity. In these language models every rule that gives attention a null removed the first-token sink and cut massive activations by 67% to 82%, as earlier reports for gates and attention biases found, and, sigmoid aside, lowered perplexity slightly at the training length; the comparison registered for two of these rules held in every seed, while the same comparison failed in the harness's vision transformers. We close with falsifiable predictions for future architectures, most of them not yet tested. This is a working draft, not a final version. It is unpolished in places, incomplete in others, and keeps exploratory material a polished paper would leave out, because that material helps decide what comes next and shows the programme's big picture more fully. items.summary: Bulk transcriptomic differences between groups reflect both altered cell composition and altered expression within cells. Methods such as csSAM, TOAST and CIBERSORTx separate the two, but all require additional information: measured per-sample proportions, anchor genes, or an external reference. We examine what can be established under a pure-bulk paired design in which none of this information is available. We formalise the decomposition obs = comp + resid and test three propositions: whether resid can be interpreted as within-cell regulation; how closely comp tracks obs, and what that agreement depends on; and whether the number of cell compartments is a well-defined model-complexity variable. Data comprise four abdominal aortic aneurysm cohorts, one lung cohort and the HLCA normal lung atlas (584,944 cells × 27,402 genes). Deconvolution uses a self-implemented Lawson–Hanson non-negative least squares validated on three problems with known answers. comp + resid = obs is an algebraic identity (same-source R² = 1.000000000000000). resid cannot be interpreted as within-cell regulation: apart from a degenerate case, the control cell-type-specific profile is not point-identifiable, and swapping reference profiles in a zero-regulation construction drives resid to −5.4654. Pearson r between comp and obs is 0.7335 (0.7001–0.8041) under platform-matched pseudo-bulk conditions, 0.2379–0.3791 across four aorta cohorts, and 0.1675–0.3019 for lung UIP/IPF; regression slopes are 0.078–0.801. A fully crossed 3 × 3 design with four aggregation weights shows that with six reference compartments r ranges from 0.2674 to 0.8417 (SD 0.239) and is not identifiable. comp is an approximate index of compositional change; resid carries no inferable information about within-cell regulation; and the number of compartments is not a well-defined model-complexity variable. --- 群体间 bulk 转录组差异同时反映细胞组成的改变与细胞内表达的改变。csSAM、TOAST、CIBERSORTx 等方法可将两者分开,但都需要额外信息:测得的逐样本比例、锚定基因,或外部参考。本文考察在上述信息全部不可得的纯 bulk 配对设计下,这一归因能做到什么程度、边界在哪里。我们形式化分解 obs = comp + resid,并检验三个命题:resid 能否解释为细胞内调控;comp 与 obs 的一致性能达到多少、依赖什么;以及「细胞区室数」是否为良定义的模型复杂度变量。数据包括四个腹主动脉瘤队列、一个肺队列,以及 HLCA 正常肺图谱(584,944 细胞 × 27,402 基因)。解卷积用自实现的 Lawson–Hanson 非负最小二乘,在三个已知答案问题上验证。comp + resid = obs 是代数恒等式(同源 R² = 1.000000000000000)。resid 不能解释为细胞内调控:除退化情形外,对照组细胞类型特异谱不可点识别;在零调控构造中对调参考谱可使 resid 达到 −5.4654。comp 与 obs 的 Pearson r:平台匹配伪 bulk 为 0.7335(0.7001–0.8041);主动脉四队列 0.2379–0.3791;肺 UIP/IPF 0.1675–0.3019。回归斜率 0.078–0.801。完全交叉的 3 × 3 设计配合四种聚合权重显示:参考区室数为 6 时 r 在 0.2674–0.8417 间摆动(SD 0.239),不可识别。comp 可作为组成变化的近似指标;resid 不承载可推断的细胞内调控信息;区室数不是良定义的模型复杂度变量。 --- This record contains the English and the Chinese version of the manuscript, both as PDF and as editable source, together with the companion manuscript on six failure modes (files 03 and 04). items.summary: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/.
items.title: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction

items.summary: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.
items.title: SPOOK: Sparse Pixel Optimization for Off-Manifold Knowledge in Vision Encoders

items.summary: Supervised pairwise graph representations convert pairwise predictive relations into sample-specific graphs, but graph-level accuracy does not by itself show that higher-order topology carries the signal. In a controlled Transformer error-detection task, supervised pairwise graphs outperform attention-as-adjacency (ROC-AUC $0.839$ versus $0.559$; the comparable no-confidence pair is $0.687$ versus $0.559$), but their apparent advantage over model confidence disappears after controlling for sequence length, which is almost perfectly recoverable from the pooled hidden state ($R^2=0.9995$). On published HCP Emotion ensemble graphs, signed node aggregation already acts as an ensemble of supervised pairwise predictions. Edge magnitude alone is near chance; topology-aware augmentations change ROC-AUC by at most $0.004$, with only sign-separated degree showing small positive changes across all tested graph sizes, while a validation-tuned three-layer GCN provides no measurable improvement over the signed node-summary baseline. A Fisher post-hoc corrector satisfies its distribution-agnostic guarantees across the evaluated feature representations and remains stable under reduced labelled budgets; in a near-error-free fMRI calibration regime the bound correctly becomes statistically uninformative. A separate cross-attention analysis identifies a redundant reversal circuit and downstream EOS-timing and copy failures. Higher-order topology should therefore be credited only after local supervised evidence and recoverable nuisance variables have been excluded.
items.title: Interpreting Supervised Pairwise Graph Representations: Local Evidence, Confounding, and Provable Post-hoc Correction

items.summary: Bounded Agentic Distribution Experiments (v0.7.0): A Reproducible Framework for Comparing Agentic Intervention Discovery with Non-Agentic Search This software implements the computational framework and pre-pilot experimental protocol associated with the research manuscript Evaluating the Incremental Value of Agentic Intervention Discovery over Non-Agentic Search in Multi-Actor Distribution Networks . The framework evaluates whether a generative AI agent can identify economically beneficial operational interventions beyond those discovered by budget-matched non-agentic search. Agentic and non-agentic methods operate within the same typed intervention space, access the same simulator information, and are subject to common evaluation budgets. Candidate interventions undergo deterministic verification of encoded structural constraints and, where applicable, stochastic qualification against economic, service, route, and actor-participation criteria. The reference environment represents a stylized print-media distribution network with 420 retailers, 18 baseline delivery vehicles, uncertain demand, allocation decisions, reverse logistics, route constraints, temporary fleet capacity, discontinuous staffing requirements, and sales-contingent remuneration. Its parameters combine industry-informed inputs, documented benchmarks, modeling assumptions, and calibration targets. The environment is intended for controlled computational evaluation rather than empirical representation of the Italian distribution industry. Experimental design Version 0.7.0 implements two frozen intervention-complexity regimes: Low-complexity regime (RL): allocation reweighting only, with a maximum intervention length of one action. Multi-domain coupled regime (RC): allocation, route transfer, temporary fleet, and forecasting interventions, with a maximum intervention length of three actions. Both regimes use a candidate-evaluation budget of 40 simulator calls. The primary comparison uses ten independent generative-agent realizations and ten independent simulated-annealing realizations per regime. The software separates proposal-mechanism randomness from simulation-scenario randomness and supports common random numbers for comparative evaluation. The statistical implementation includes regime-specific pilot sizing, independent within-method repetition resampling, shared scenario resampling, and a two-dimensional bootstrap for confirmatory inference. Final-test selection follows a frozen rule combining precision requirements from both regimes with the minimum-detectable-effect requirement for the multi-domain superiority hypothesis. These tests examine computational correctness, reproducibility, regime restrictions, seed handling, bootstrap procedures, and experimental locking. They do not establish empirical agent performance. This release corresponds to the frozen pre-pilot protocol BAD-420-v0.7-2026-09-11 . The final-test set remains locked until a valid pilot mechanically determines its size. No live API-based agent-performance experiment or confirmatory comparison is included in this release. Consequently, the software does not establish that agentic intervention discovery outperforms, matches, or underperforms non-agentic search. items.summary: Nine years after its introduction, the transformer remains the default sequence model. The usual explanations are real: parallel matrix multiplication on accelerators, predictable returns to scale, a co-evolved ecosystem and exact recall from an uncompressed context. But they do not explain why most modifications barely move accuracy, which properties are essential, why the changes practice adopted took the forms they did, or where the design can still move. This paper is the entry point to a collection of papers that treat a token-mixing layer as an averaging operator rebuilt from its own input and iterated through depth. Such a layer faces six failure modes (collapse to consensus, contamination of content by routing, runaway feedback, the inability to abstain, dilution as context grows, and the inability to represent direction). Each has a protection, proved within a declared class, and a signature measured at small scale when that protection is removed; for gain control, which protects against runaway feedback, that signature is synthetic. We read softmax attention in a pre-normalized residual block as the one known point where all six protections are cheap at once under the prices of parallel hardware and gradient descent; this is an interpretation, not a measured optimum. Two mechanisms, measured at small scale, help explain why its neighbourhood is flat: trained networks compensate local deficits through spare capacity, and, in ten scored tests, making a protection explicit did not beat a block that already supplies it. The anchor, the residual or input path that protects against collapse to consensus, is the one protection whose loss compensation provably cannot repair: under strict mixing, where repeated averaging contracts token differences toward zero, no extra capacity of bounded gain (bounded sensitivity) brings back what is lost without it, and in small-model ablations nothing else in the block made up for it. This is a proved bound; a trained test that adds capacity is pending. Many changes adopted in the mixing layer and its block since 2017, among them pre-normalization, QK-norm, sinks and output gates, read as re-supplies of the same protections; the account is silent on others, such as changes to the MLP. The room that remains for the design to move is where a protection is patched (met only by a fix that works over a limited range, such as the trained length) or paid at a price that another design could avoid. It includes abstention and retrieval at long context, governed by a two-sided log-N law in the context length (with bounded scores, no fixed rule for abstaining keeps both as the context grows), and bounded memory, whose price for exact recall is a per-head capacity. It also includes decisions that sum over all competitors where reading the largest would do, and the writer of new features (in a transformer, the MLP and the output map), for which the collection has no theory yet of what a good writer computes. Along the way the collection establishes results that stand on their own: attention has an arrow that default statistics of a single operator cannot see; depth is a distribution over path lengths; converged adaptive averaging can amplify changes in its input and overturn correct predictions; and softmax obeys length laws that decisions on maxima escape while the competing scores stay below the decision's threshold. We state what is proved, what is measured, what is interpretation, and what is still pending. This is a working draft, not a final version. items.summary: Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI This repository contains the full simulator, notebooks, configuration files, and result checkpoints for the paper “Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI: Outage Control and Sensing-Information Preservation.” The method, SR-CBSA, is a scenario-robust coordinated block successive convex approximation scheme for joint communication and sensing beamforming in distributed cell-free massive MIMO ISAC networks under pilot-based CSI uncertainty. It enforces direct global received-signal SINR constraints over sampled channel-error scenarios, preserves target-directed sensing power and a transmit-side azimuth-information surrogate, and stabilizes sequential per-access-point updates through trust regions, damping, proximal regularization, and penalized feasibility slack. Training, held-out validation, the physical true channel, and unseen-error test scenarios are kept strictly separate, so the reported gains reflect genuine robustness rather than overfitting to the sampled errors. The code reproduces every result in the paper from seed-controlled experiments: the paired Monte Carlo study across 5, 10, 15, and 20 dB pilot SNR, the same-realization method comparison, the QoS-target feasibility sweep, the responsibility-rule ablation, the scenario-count and synchronization-error sensitivity studies, the full-rank and locally low-rank scalability cases, and the baseline comparisons including the adapted JointOpt framework and a feasible max-min robust SOCP relaxation. All optimization uses CVXPY with CLARABEL, runs on CPU, and writes CSV checkpoints so long runs can be resumed and verified independently. Set the experiment flags in the configuration cell, run the notebook top to bottom, and the module and figures are regenerated automatically. See the README for environment setup, the flag-to-experiment mapping, and the fixed seeds used for each reported table and figure.
items.title: Scenario-Robust Coordinated Beamforming for Cell-Free ISAC under Imperfect CSI: Outage Control and Sensing-Information Preservation

items.summary: Photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) underpin critical applications in telecommunications, sensing, and high-power laser delivery, yet their design remains a manual, expert-intensive process that couples geometric intuition with deep waveguide physics. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising path toward automating PCF design, but can they truly reason about photonic physics from microscopy images, or do they merely recognize visual patterns? We introduce PCFBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs on the perception, reasoning, and decision steps of the photonic inverse-design loop. PCFBench spans 26 tasks organized into six categories of increasing cognitive demand (Geometry Perception, Physics Understanding, Text Generation, Multi-modal Reasoning, Inverse-Design Decision, and Code Generation), built from over 220K FDTD simulation samples across 18 structurally diverse fiber families. We evaluate both individual VLMs on isolated tasks and multi-agent systems (MAS) on the full sequential pipeline from perception to design. Our results reveal a striking perception-design gap: current models can identify fiber geometry with moderate success, yet consistently fail to translate that visual understanding into physics-aware design actions. Moreover, cascading agents through the pipeline exposes significant error propagation, where upstream perception mistakes compound into downstream design failures. These findings suggest that neither model scaling nor naive agent chaining suffices, and that closing the loop demands explicit physical grounding. PCFBench provides the community with a rigorous, multi-dimensional testbed to measure progress toward AI-assisted photonic engineering. The project is available at https://pcfbench.github.io/.
items.title: PCFBench: How Far Can Large Vision-Language Models Go in Physics-aware Photonic Inverse Design?

items.summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on role-specific prompts and execution models to solve complex tasks collaboratively. However, prompt optimization typically keeps model assignments fixed, leaving differences in role requirements and their associated inference costs outside the search. We present UniMASO, a Unified framework for heterogeneous Multi-Agent System Optimization through the joint adaptation of prompts and model assignments. UniMASO evaluates candidate updates through local, downstream, and global feedback, using cost-aware Pareto search to retain useful quality-cost trade-offs. Topology-aware co-evolution then coordinates these updates according to agent roles and dependencies. Cross-level trajectory memory further supplies historical successes and failures to guide subsequent optimization. Experiments on five benchmarks and five execution topologies show that UniMASO achieves competitive task performance at substantially lower deployment cost than the strongest homogeneous configurations. Under centralized execution, it improves the average score from 69.79 to 70.40 while reducing token-weighted deployment cost by 85.2% relative to DeepSeek-V4-Pro with MASPO. These results support joint prompt-model adaptation as an effective approach to efficient multi-agent collaboration. The code is available at https://github.com/Achilles008/UniMASO_main.
items.title: Not Every Agent Needs the Strongest Model: Unified Prompt-Model Optimization for Heterogeneous LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length $L$ and age threshold $T$ satisfy $L\ge T>N\ge2$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.
items.title: AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems

items.summary: TEMPLATE-DIRECTED MASS FABRICATION OF BIOMEDICAL MICRO/NANOROBOTS AT THE LIMIT is a 770-page, high-density English research monograph on scaling template replication without losing dimensional fidelity, surface integrity, functional consistency or scientific traceability. The book treats the template as a stateful manufacturing ancestor rather than a passive tool. Every cavity and replication cycle is registered so that template wear, release-coating decay, demolding force, replica bias, particle residue, spatial defect clustering and functional outcomes can be linked across the full template life. Its central falsifiable claim asks whether lifetime-aware monitoring can predict rising defect probability before damage spreads. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates cover cavity filling, squeeze flow, material relaxation, cure conversion, shrinkage, residual stress, adhesion, demolding, fracture, Archard wear, coating survival, hidden wear states, geometry transfer, Hausdorff error, spatial point processes, defect ancestry, survival hazards, change points, capability, conservative yield, hierarchical variance and qualified-part cost. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the monograph develops replication physics, release mechanics, template wear, spatial defect genealogy, adaptive process control, functional qualification, lifecycle economics and independent transfer. Two hundred Research Gates define blind challenges, strong comparators, evidence packages, hard stops and successor forks. items.summary: Collective behavior in biological systems emerges through adaptive interactions among units, enabling large populations to coordinate without centralized control. This mechanism raises the question of whether collective behavior in engineered multi-agent systems can likewise be regulated by modifying the interaction law between agents, rather than by directly controlling individual units. To answer this question, we consider large-scale multi-agent systems evolving on a ring and treat the interaction kernel as a time-varying control variable whose evolution regulates the collective dynamics. Using a mean-field formulation, we develop a framework for the analysis and design of kernel-based controllers. We derive explicit conditions for controllability in application-relevant scenarios, and synthesize a state-feedback controller to regulate the kernel dynamics, validated on the microscopic, discrete dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate the approach's effectiveness and robustness to unmodeled perturbations. This work constitutes a first step in the design of bio-inspired control strategies for large-scale multi-agent systems by modulation of interactions between agents.
items.title: Density control of large-scale multi-agent systems via tuning of agent interactions

items.summary: Training large language models (LLMs) in sub-8-bit arithmetic promises substantial gains in memory bandwidth and compute throughput, yet FP4 formats introduce quantization error severe enough to destabilize optimization if left unaddressed. We present ALTO, an open-source training recipe for GPT-OSS-20B, a 20-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, on the MLPerf Small MoE Training benchmark under the MXFP4 microscaling format. The recipe combines established techniques from Abecassis, Felix et al. [arXiv:2509.25149] (hybrid 1D/2D block quantization, randomized Hadamard transforms, and stochastic rounding) with a simplified weight de-oscillation scheme adapted from TetraJet-v2 [arXiv:2510.27527]. On C4 validation at global batch size 16, MXFP4 + RHT + SR + de-oscillation reaches a validation loss of 3.3350 at 16,128 steps, only 0.007 above the BF16 baseline (3.3283), closing roughly 50% of the gap left by MXFP4 without de-oscillation (3.3418). Measured by steps to reach the MLPerf quality target (validation loss 3.34), de-oscillation cuts the FP4 convergence overhead relative to BF16 from +20.0% to +5.0%. We also report negative end-to-end results from differential gradient estimation, outlier clipping, and macro-block scaling, despite each showing operator-level SNR gains. All experiments use simulated MXFP4 kernels on AMD MI300 hardware and wall-clock speed has not been optimized.
items.title: Training an MoE LLM in MXFP4: How We Closed the Gap to BF16

items.summary: Existing evaluation protocols for unit tests rely on aggregate metrics such as branch coverage and mutation score. These metrics quantify the extent to which a test suite exercises program behavior, but do not identify the behavioral obligations it systematically leaves unchecked. We propose BlindSpotEval, an obligation-based evaluation framework aligned with the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern. The framework comprises three metrics, Boundary-Value Adequacy, Control-Flow Adequacy, and Oracle Strength, complemented by an assessment of execution reliability. We also introduce ObligBench, a complexity-stratified Java benchmark comprising 895 complex and 700 low-complexity functions with source-side obligation annotations. Evaluating 14,320 tests from four LLMs under four prompting strategies reveals systematic blind spots. Incorrect assertions account for 15.6% of test failures, illustrating that coverage alone does not establish oracle correctness. Among executable tests, coverage of null, negative, and empty arguments reaches only 34.8%, 23.8%, and 38.8%, compared with average coverage above 93% for booleans. Catch blocks and default groups have Control-Flow Adequacy scores of only 0.100 and 0.312. Across both dimensions, LLM-generated tests exhibit the happy-path bias observed in human-written tests, concentrating on normal inputs and expected flows while leaving unusual values and exceptional paths unchecked. Oracle strength is high on average but uneven, with weaker assertions for object return property values and exceptions. These blind spots also occur in low-complexity functions, suggesting that code complexity alone does not explain them. BlindSpotEval provides construct-level adequacy profiles that identify under-tested obligation types and can guide targeted improvements beyond those supported by aggregate scores alone.
items.title: Beyond Coverage and Mutation: A Blind-Spot Analysis of LLM-Generated Unit Tests

items.summary: University technical festivals combine event discovery, registration, payment collection, venue attendance, certification, feedback, and reporting in one workflow, yet they are commonly handled through disconnected forms, spreadsheets, and payment dashboards. This paper presents the design, implementation, and functional verification of Supernova 2.0, a web-based event management platform deployed for the School of Engineering and Technology, MGM University, for a festival held on 4–5 September 2026 with nine flagship competitions. The system is a lightweight PHP/MySQL monolith that binds registration to server-side Razorpay payment verification, records physical venue attendance against the same participant identity, and gates certificate access on that attendance record. Administrative, organizer, and finance duties are separated through role-based access control, and a spreadsheet import path admits offline attendance records. Security controls include CSRF tokens, password hashing, session regeneration, login throttling, prepared statements, security headers, and HMAC signature verification. Validation is functional and workflow-oriented; no performance benchmark, usability study, or penetration test was performed, and no quantitative results are reported. The contribution is the integration of established mechanisms into a single working workflow in a focused, single-event institutional deployment.
items.title: An Integrated Event Management System for a University

items.summary: Websites and applications deploy CAPTCHAs and anti-automation mechanisms that use behavioral signals such as interaction trajectories and timing, not outcomes alone, to distinguish humans from automated agents. We call these protected GUI environments, where correctly solving a verification task is insufficient for end-to-end task completion. Agents must turn solver outputs into accepted interactions and adapt execution to runtime feedback under time constraints. We introduce SolveBind, a GUI-agent framework combining hierarchical solving with runtime supervision. A hierarchical solving tree decomposes verification into interdependent Perceive, Ground, Solve, Act, and Verify capabilities. A runtime supervisor grounds action commitments in tool-derived evidence, revises them as evidence arrives, and mediates execution under explicit recovery budgets. Across nine CAPTCHA task families and nine backbone models, SolveBind achieves the highest success rate on eight backbones, outperforming the strongest baseline by 13.3-34.5 percentage points. It achieves the highest success rate on all six AndroidWorld backbones. In a paired GPT-5.5 analysis, MobileAgent produces correct answers but fails dynamic verification on 13 of 90 tasks; SolveBind succeeds on seven of these tasks. With automatic submission, removing binding reduces success from 82.22% to 71.56% and increases latency and token usage. Recovery caps reduce execution cost with a small observed success trade-off: removing them raises success from 82.22% to 83.56%, while increasing latency and token usage to 3.7x and 2.4x their full-supervision values, respectively. These results support evidence-grounded execution control while identifying a success-cost trade-off in recovery and failure boundaries of heuristic submission rules.
items.title: Correct Answers, Closed Gates: SolveBind for GUI Agents at the Verification Barrier

items.summary: The Quantum Internet is commonly envisioned as a network that transports quantum states and distributes entanglement as the key resource underpinning distributed quantum applications. This view is necessary but incomplete if quantum phenomena are confined to what the network carries or manages, while network functionalities remain grounded predominantly in classical abstractions. This Perspective advances a broader thesis: quantum phenomena can also participate directly in the realization of network functionalities. We first establish the architectural baseline by introducing entanglement as a stateful network resource whose operational condition is non-locally distributed across remote nodes, evolves through manipulation or consumption, and degrades over time through decoherence. Its evolving state must therefore remain visible to the functionalities acting on it. We then move beyond resource visibility and use two mechanisms as proof points of a broader quantum-native functional design space: entanglement generation during propagation through coherent spatial-path superposition, and operational connectivity induced by shared entanglement that can depart from the physical graph. These examples show that paths, neighbors, or participating nodes may become operationally relevant in ways determined by quantum coherence and shared entanglement, rather than by physical connectivity alone. We identify Quantum Addressing as a transversal abstraction capable of representing such relations while complementing, rather than replacing, classical addressing and signaling. The resulting perspective broadens the Quantum Internet from transporting quantum information and distributing entanglement to exploiting quantum phenomena in network functioning, opening a coupled frontier spanning routing, forwarding, control, and functionality placement.
items.title: Beyond Quantum Messages: Toward Quantum-Native Network Functioning
